doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: Herbie Mann, Junior Mance and Sonny Sharrock dates
summary: Laws remembers a Herbie Mann session at Rudy Van Gelder's but not others. He recalls Sonny Sharrock's distortion and mourns the many CTI colleagues who have died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Then the next one that shows up in the discography is in July of ’67. That’s Glory of Love, Herbie Mann’s date.
Right. I remember that date. That was at Rudy Van Gelder’s. I think Herbie invited me to play. I’m not sure. I can’t remember for sure.
It’s his date.
Yeah, I think he invited me to do that. At that time, I think I had a copy of it, but I don’t think I have it now.
Doing Ray Charles, Unchain My Heart.
Oh really? I don’t have much recollection of that date.
Then Junior Mance.
I played with him too?
Um-hmm. I Believe to My Soul is the title of the record.
God, I don’t recall that at all. Sorry.
Like I said, 333 titles. I’d be amazed if you did remember it all.

Then there’s another one, Herbie Mann. This is a larger group. I’m not sure if it’s released under the same title. It must have been, because you’re on – here’s an interesting one, again under Herbie Mann: Herbie Mann, yourself, Roy Ayers, Sonny Sharrock on guitar, Earl May on bass, Grady Tate, drums, Ray Barretto, percussion. The Letter, again doing some more pop stuff. Hold On, I’m Comin’.
Hmm. I’m on that, too?
Any recollection of that?
Uh-uh. I have no recall, no recollection of that.
Okay. I was just going to ask about Sonny Sharrock, because . . .
I remember Sonny Sharrock. He played with a lot of distortion on his guitar. That’s all I can remember. A lot of – he played with Herbie Mann’s, and he played with a lot – is he still alive?
No. Sonny’s gone.
A lot of those guys are gone. Eric Gale.
Yeah, Richard Tee is gone.
Richard Tee, all these guys. Thanks for reminding me of that. Yeah, a lot of those guys are dead. Those CTI records. They’re gone.
